tests.title: Equipment Desk starts blank and authors schema and forms through supported controls

requirements.text: A reviewer can trace every requirement and checklist case to a run, source revision, fixture, expected result, observed result and retained evidence; pending/skipped/failed never count as passed.
An author can create, configure, generate, run and reopen Workshop Planner through Studio from an empty workspace and a missing chosen folder.
An author can create Library Catalog through Studio and connect an existing-database variant without inspection/Cancel changing that database.
An author can create tables, scalar types, primary/foreign/unique keys in the reusable editor, revisit it later, review a safe schema change and observe only its declared effects.
The proposed pages, access and flow preview correspond to the completed editable Page → Form → Control objects; edits and flow/settings shortcuts reopen the correct project.
Names resolve to stable keys, parent links filter the correct children, and Add/login/Save/Cancel preserve typed parent context while preselecting only new-record fields.
Create/edit/delete support clear validation, uniqueness and related-record errors, confirmations naming the record, Cancel without writes and no partial rows after failed actions.
Public browsing remains public; protected pages and direct write handlers reject anonymous use; login/logout and validated return targets behave consistently across sessions/tabs.
Authors can build the declared joins, counts, exact totals, zero-child handling and runtime thresholds through the query/report UI, with independently checked results before and after data changes.

Two regenerations per application preserve all business rows, schema/query/report/access/navigation settings, and declared authored module bytes; source conflicts block safe promotion until explicitly resolved.
An author can inspect generated source and declare/edit one supported authored extension through Studio, observe its behavior, and retain it through regeneration.
A reviewer can install, build, test and run the generated/exported app with Studio stopped, explicit private configuration, intact data and visitor identity, and no embedded author capability.
Schema/query/page/control drafts survive the documented switch/reload recovery paths and unrelated revision notifications without silent value, focus, caret or project-ownership changes.

Stale revisions, duplicate requests, changed database identity, invalid paths/context, failed runtime starts and interrupted reviewed operations yield actionable status and recover without unrelated writes or false success.
A bounded MCP/direct-command smoke uses the same validation, revision, idempotency and authorization semantics as Studio; it cannot substitute for UI acceptance or bypass boundaries.
Both complete journeys run twice consecutively from fresh private workspaces without hidden repairs, retries masking failures, application-specific generator branches or manual test-data corrections.
Each observed blocker is reproduced, fixed generically where appropriate, regression-tested and rerun; the final verdict lists passing requirements and any explicitly justified nonblocking deferrals.
Before/after comparisons show zero unintended changes to business rows, declared authored bytes and unrelated project/draft state after success, rejection and recovery cases.
Every anonymous direct-write and invalid-origin/return/path case in the checklist is rejected; retained public artifacts contain zero real secrets or private user-study data.
Both fresh complete journeys pass twice consecutively with zero retries and zero forced expected-failure conversions; any infrastructure failure is reported separately and rerun explicitly.

At the bounded fixture sizes (at most 200 rows/table and 12 tables/project), p95 local editing/navigation feedback is within 2 seconds over 30 interactions; valid Save completes within 5 seconds on the recorded reference machine, excluding external dependency acquisition and builds.
Across 30 unrelated-notification/view-switch interactions with an active draft, zero unintended text replacements, caret resets, lost edits, duplicate controls or wrong-project saves occur.
Every mandatory acceptance case and every FR/NFR/C has a disposition and source-linked evidence in the final report; no unresolved critical/high defect is present.
Retain the existing SQLite and TypeScript/Next.js target, supported Linux environment and pinned tooling; no framework, dependency or Spec Kitty upgrades are required by this mission.
PR #1 and existing Workshop Planner/other private studies are baselines; destructive testing uses fresh isolated copies, never the user's working studies.

Normal application definitions, schemas, queries, access, navigation and authored source are configured in Studio. Documented install/build/run/environment preparation and supplied raw existing-database fixtures are allowed; direct API/model edits cannot repair a UI journey and still count as its pass.

Repair issues needed for the declared checklist; keep unsupported features explicit. No new targets, hosted service, deployment, complete visual redesign, arbitrary control runtime, large-lookup browser or composite lookup widget is included.
Lifecycle scripts stay disabled; private configuration, databases, identity stores and unredacted browser traces stay outside tracked evidence; historical reports remain intact.
Prior test counts and approved packages are context, not proof of this mission. Evaluate the exact final revision; distinguish local checks, hosted checks and unverified external conditions.
